questions.q: What opens the Global Actions menu in Lightning Experience?
options: The plus icon in the header
questions.explain: The plus icon in the header opens Global Actions, available from anywhere in the org.

questions.q: What is required to use a Global Action?
options: The user must already be viewing a specific record
The action must be attached to a Case object
No record context is required — it's available from anywhere
The user must be a System Administrator
questions.explain: Global Actions need no record context — that's exactly what distinguishes them from object-specific actions.

questions.q: Why do actions like 'Submit for Approval' or 'Change Owner' show up on a record's overflow menu but not in Global Actions?
options: They only make sense in the context of a specific record already open — they're object-specific
Global Actions can't include more than 5 items
They require a custom Lightning component
questions.explain: Object-specific actions are scoped to one object type and the record context already on screen.

questions.q: What is a 'quick action,' per this lesson?
options: A shortcut form with fewer fields than the full record, built for speed
questions.explain: A quick action, global or object-specific, is a streamlined shortcut form — not the full record edit screen.

questions.q: What controls which Global Actions a given user profile actually sees?
questions.explain: The publisher layout determines which global actions are visible to users on a given profile.
